intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is caused by heterozygous or homozygous mutation in the LEF1 gene on chromosome 4q25.

paragraphs.text: Ectodermal dysplasia-17 with or without limb malformations (ECTD17) is a disorder caused by variants in LEF1. Its features include ectodermal dysplasia, with severe oligodontia, hypotrichosis, and hypohidrosis, and various limb malformations, such as radial ray defects, polydactyly, or split hand/foot. Inheritance can be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive, depending on the type and location of the LEF1 variant (Lévy et al., 2020; Dufour et al., 2022).

paragraphs.text: In 2 unrelated patients with hypohidrotic ectodermal dysplasia, Lévy et al. (2020) identified de novo deletions at chromosome 4q25 that encompassed the LEF1 gene. They proposed that LEF1 haploinsufficiency causes ectodermal dysplasia and noted that no pathogenic variants involving LEF1 had previously been reported in humans.

paragraphs.text: Using high-throughput sequencing, Dufour et al. (2022) detected monoallelic LEF1 variants in 11 affected individuals from 4 unrelated families, and a biallelic LEF1 variant in an affected individual from a consanguineous family. They studied the cellular consequences of the variants with immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, pulldown assays, and/or RNA sequencing. Their functional data pointed to 2 molecular mechanisms. Haploinsufficiency or loss of DNA binding was associated with a mild to moderate phenotype, whereas loss of beta-catenin binding caused by biallelic variants was associated with a severe phenotype. Transcriptomic studies showed altered WNT signaling.
